_purpose: Defines the runnable agent interaction: what an agent-participant is shown, what it must produce, how condition assignment works, and how outputs map back to materials.json. task/adapter.py implements this contract.
network_access: none required or permitted at runtime
participant_role: The agent plays the role of a single human survey/experiment participant. Each invocation of adapter.py administers exactly one (study, condition) cell to one simulated participant and returns one structured response record. To reproduce the paper's group-level statistics, the harness must invoke adapter.py many times per condition (matching or approximating the original per-condition n's in study.json) and pass the collected records to evaluation/evaluation.py.

steps.format: two percentages summing to 100, one per own_choice_options entry
for each trait, two ratings in [-50,50]: one for the typical person choosing option 1, one for option 2, using trait_scale_template

studies.label: 35-item (34 usable) self/peer categorization questionnaire
studies.design: within-subjects; all usable items shown to every participant
studies.note: Order (self-categorize first vs. peer-estimate first) had no reported effect in the original study; both conditions are offered for completeness but adapter.py defaults to self_first.
excluded_items: Political expectations: Expects removal of Nixon from office

steps.format: for each of the 34 usable items, which of category_1/category_2 applies to the participant
for each item, estimated % of 'college students in general' who fall in category_1

studies.label: Hypothetical sandwich-board-sign story (2 sign versions)
studies.design: between-subjects; one sign version per participant

steps.format: for each of the 8 traits, ratings in [-50,50] for the typical person who would wear vs. not wear the sign

studies.label: Text-reconstructed real-choice sandwich-board scenario
studies.design: between-subjects; sign-version not specified by the paper for Study 4 (only Study 3 varied the sign text) — adapter.py uses a single generic administration
studies.blocking_reason: The original Study 4 manipulation depended on a live experimenter, a real 30-minute campus walk, and genuine deception/debriefing — none of which a text-only agent task can faithfully reproduce. This condition administers the same textual materials (cover story + Likes/Dislikes vignettes) and records a stated hypothetical choice; it is NOT a behavioral replication and must be reported as such, never conflated with the original 'real choice' data.

steps.note: randomize which of Version A/B is presented as 'agreed' vs 'refused', per study4.target_person_pairing_note

steps.format: for each of the 8 assumed traits, ratings in [-50,50] for each of the two target persons
steps.caveat: study4.traits.evidence_label is 'missing' — trait list is an assumption carried over from Study 3, not confirmed for Study 4

own_choice.description: for study1/study3/study4: which option the participant personally picked; for study2: N/A at record level (per-item in self_category)

consensus_estimate.description: for study1/study3/study4: {option: percentage} summing to 100; for study2: per-item peer_estimate_pct list

trait_ratings.description: trait -> {option_or_target: rating in [-50,50]}, omitted for study2

condition_assignment.method: uniform random over the study's listed conditions unless the caller pins a condition via --study/--condition CLI flags
condition_assignment.rationale: matches the original studies' between-subjects random assignment to story/sign version

outputs.single_run_record: one JSON object per adapter.py invocation, matching response_schema, written to stdout or --out-file
outputs.aggregate_input_for_evaluation: a JSON-lines file of many single_run_records (one participant each), passed to evaluation/evaluation.py
